mainTopic: Redeeming the extra שתי הלחם loaves, extra loaves and sheep on שבועות, and the rule of 'sin so that you may gain'
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: when extra loaves were brought with the שבועות sheep, the extra loaves are eaten after פדיון. The רבנן ask רב חסדא how this can fit רבי, who holds that שחיטה makes the loaves fully holy. Redeeming outside the עזרה would make the holy loaves פסול as יוצא, and redeeming inside seems to bring חולין into the עזרה. רב חסדא answers that it is done inside, because the loaves become חולין on their own and nobody brought them in. A ברייתא saying redemption happens only outside is assigned to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Next, the גמרא checks whether the ברייתא refutes רבי יוחנן about a תודה with eighty loaves, and answers with רבי זירא: everyone agrees when the owner said which loaves should become holy. Then רבי חנינא טירתא teaches that if four sheep were slaughtered for the two loaves, two are sprinkled שלא לשמן so the others are not lost. רבי יוחנן objects that we don't say 'sin so that you may gain'. The answers limit that rule to the same offering and the same day. The amud ends with a new challenge from a משנה about a broken barrel of תרומה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The extra loaves are eaten through redemption
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the ברייתא: the remaining loaves may be eaten once they are redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rest of the loaves are eaten through redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא that started earlier. It says the loaves that are not needed are eaten after they are redeemed with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of the loaves are used for the offering, and the rest are not needed. The ברייתא says those extra loaves can lose their holiness through פדיון and then be eaten. The whole discussion that follows is about how this פדיון could work.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: moving the holiness of an item onto money, so the item becomes ordinary
And the rest (the leftover loaves)
Are eaten

phrases.english: And the rest are eaten through redemption.
phrases.notes: 'The rest' means the extra loaves, from the ברייתא quoted just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that was quoted before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra loaves can be eaten after being redeemed.

steps.title: The רבנן claim the ברייתא does not follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רב חסדא that this ברייתא cannot match the opinion of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said this before רב חסדא: This ברייתא is not in line with רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars bring a claim to רב חסדא: this ברייתא does not fit רבי's opinion. The next steps explain why they think so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that once the sheep are slaughtered, the loaves become fully holy (קדושת הגוף). Fully holy items cannot simply be redeemed. Here two of the loaves are fully holy and we don't know which, so redeeming 'the rest' seems to cause a problem for רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in his presence
This is not in line with... (this source doesn't match a certain opinion)

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Ḥisda:
This is not in accordance with Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא הָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which opinion the ברייתא from step 1 follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the ברייתא could follow רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redemption of the extra loaves seems impossible under רבי's view that שחיטה makes the loaves fully holy.

steps.title: If it follows רבי, where would the redemption happen?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי holds שחיטה makes the loaves holy, the רבנן ask where the redeeming would take place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it is רבי, since he says the slaughter makes the loaves holy, when he redeems them, where does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars start explaining their claim by asking a pointed question: where could the loaves be redeemed? This sets up the two options in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the שחיטה already made two of the loaves fully holy. To free the other two, one would redeem all four with the condition that 'whichever are not fully holy are redeemed.' The question is about place: where can this be done without causing a problem?

keyTerms.meaning: The slaughter (of the sheep) makes the loaves holy
That he redeems
Where?

phrases.english: For if it is Rabbi,
since he says slaughter consecrates,
that he redeems them, where?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי רַבִּי כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר שְׁחִיטָה מְקַדְּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining why the ברייתא can't follow רבי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location where the redemption of the loaves could happen under רבי's view.

steps.title: Outside or inside, both options cause a problem
steps.stepSummary: Redeeming outside the עזרה makes the holy loaves פסול as יוצא; redeeming inside brings חולין into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he redeems them outside, since it is written 'before ה׳,' they become פסול by leaving. If inside, he is bringing non-holy items into the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars show that every choice fails. Outside ruins the holy loaves, and inside creates a different problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside: the פסוק says the loaves are waved 'לפני ה׳', so the two fully holy loaves must stay in the עזרה; taking them out makes them פסול as יוצא. Inside: once the two other loaves are redeemed they are חולין, and having חולין in the עזרה is forbidden. So the ברייתא, which allows פדיון, can't follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: From outside (outside the עזרה)
Before ה׳: the loaves belong in the holy area
Disqualified because a holy item left its required area
Inside
Non-holy items in the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with 'inside' is not about the holy loaves. It is about the two loaves that become חולין after the redemption and are now ordinary bread inside the עזרה.

phrases.english: If he redeems them outside,
since it is written "before the Lord,"
they are disqualified by leaving.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two loaves that are truly holy. Taking them out of the עזרה ruins them.

phrases.english: If inside,
he is bringing non-sacred items into the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'where?' question by showing both places lead to a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא could follow רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no place where the redemption could happen without either making the holy loaves פסול or bringing חולין into the עזרה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: It follows רבי, and the loaves become חולין on their own
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the ברייתא can follow רבי. The redemption is done inside, and that is not counted as bringing חולין in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: Really it follows רבי, and he redeems them inside. The non-holy loaves just became non-holy by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the scholars and rescues the ברייתא for רבי. He picks the 'inside' option and explains why it is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on bringing חולין into the עזרה. These loaves were holy when they came in, and they only turned into חולין later, right where they were. Since nobody brought ordinary bread in, there is no violation.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: keeping the original idea despite the question
By itself, on its own, without someone actively doing it
They become

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on חולין in the עזרה is about actively bringing ordinary items in. Something that was holy when it entered and became חולין there on its own does not break this rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the ברייתא in line with רבי's view that שחיטה makes the loaves holy. It also teaches how far the ban on חולין in the עזרה reaches.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to them:
Actually, it is in accordance with Rabbi,
and he redeems them inside,
and they become non-sacred by themselves.
phrases.notes: He means the loaves were already inside while still holy. Nobody carried ordinary bread in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְעוֹלָם כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 4 by choosing 'inside' and removing the חולין problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the prohibition: only actively bringing חולין in is forbidden, not items that become חולין on their own.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Redeeming inside counts as bringing חולין into the עזרה, so the ברייתא can't follow רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The loaves become חולין on their own inside, which is allowed, so the ברייתא can follow רבי.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the loaves are redeemed only outside
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב חסדא's claim that the redemption happens inside the עזרה. He cites a ברייתא that says the loaves are redeemed only outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But a ברייתא teaches that when he redeems the loaves, he redeems them only outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash directly with רב חסדא's answer in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that according to רבי, the loaves are redeemed inside the עזרה. This ברייתא says plainly that the redemption happens only outside. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeems them, meaning he transfers their holiness onto money
Outside the עזרה, the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But isn't it taught: when he redeems them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the extra loaves from step 1 that are going to be redeemed.

phrases.english: he redeems them only outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 5 using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that, according to רבי, the redemption is done inside the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא says the redemption happens only outside, which contradicts doing it inside.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the ברייתא requiring redemption outside must follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. According to רבי, taking the loaves out would make them פסול as יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is certainly the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. If it followed רבי, the loaves would already be פסול for having left the עזרה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the ברייתא saying the loaves are redeemed outside cannot follow רבי. It follows a different תנא, so it does not contradict רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the loaves are already holy, so taking them out would make them פסול as יוצא. That ברייתא must follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that שחיטה does not make the loaves holy, so carrying them out does no harm. רב חסדא was only explaining רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Something holy that left its required area and became פסול
They became disqualified
This is certainly

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different ברייתות here. One allows redemption, and רב חסדא explained it according to רבי. The other says redemption happens only outside, and that one follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: הָא וַדַּאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא,
phrases.english: This is certainly Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
because if it were Rabbi,
they would already be disqualified as having gone out!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא וַדַּאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge by assigning that ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (אוקימתא by author)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requiring redemption outside seemed to apply to everyone, including רבי
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, so רב חסדא's explanation of רבי stands

steps.title: Does the ברייתא refute רבי יוחנן about eighty loaves?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא suggests that the ברייתא, which says two of the four loaves become holy, refutes רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן holds that a תודה slaughtered with eighty loaves does not make even forty of them holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא said to רב אשי: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי יוחנן? It was stated: if one slaughtered a תודה with eighty loaves, חזקיה says forty of the eighty become holy, and רבי יוחנן says not even forty of the eighty become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. The ברייתא says two of the four loaves become holy, and that seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's ruling about a תודה with double the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תודה needs forty loaves. רבי יוחנן says that if it was slaughtered with eighty, none become holy. The ברייתא here says that when the כבשים were slaughtered with four loaves instead of two, two do become holy. That matches חזקיה, so it looks like a תיובתא against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation of an אמורא's view
A thanksgiving offering, brought together with forty loaves
Loaves
They became holy
Shall we say? This introduces a suggested conclusion

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Shall we say this is a refutation of Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא's ruling that when four loaves were slaughtered instead of two, two of them become holy.

phrases.english: from what was stated:
a thanks offering that one slaughtered with eighty loaves,
phrases.notes: Only forty are needed, so this is double the amount.

phrases.aramaic: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים,
phrases.english: Chizkiya says: forty out of the eighty become holy,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ אַרְבָּעִים מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan says: forty out of the eighty do not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question by comparing the ברייתא to the מחלוקת of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that none of the eighty loaves become holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says two out of four loaves become holy, which is the same situation as forty out of eighty. That fits חזקיה and contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Everyone agrees when he said which loaves should become holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבי זירא: everyone, even רבי יוחנן, agrees the loaves become holy when the owner said 'let forty of the eighty become holy.' The ברייתא is talking about a case where he said 'let two of the four become holy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it stated on this: רבי זירא said that everyone agrees that where he said 'let forty out of the eighty become holy,' they do become holy. Here too, the case is where he said 'let two out of the four become holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. It narrows the ברייתא to a case that רבי יוחנן also agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling applies only when the owner said nothing special. Then none of the loaves become holy. If the owner said up front that only forty of the eighty should become holy, everyone agrees they do. The ברייתא is read as that kind of case, with two out of four, so there is no refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees, even the opinion that seemed to disagree
Let them become holy
Two out of four

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's rule that none of the extra loaves become holy applies only when nothing was specified. If the owner said that only the required number should become holy, they do, and the ברייתא about four loaves is that kind of case.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about it,
Rabbi Zeira said: everyone agrees
where he said, "Let forty out of the eighty become holy,"
that they become holy,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי דְּאָמַר ״לִיקְדְּשׁוּ תַּרְתֵּי מִתּוֹךְ אַרְבַּע״.
phrases.english: here too, it is where he said, "Let two out of the four become holy."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן by narrowing the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to where the owner specified
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe an ordinary case with extra loaves, against רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes a case where he said 'let two of the four become holy,' and רבי יוחנן agrees with that

steps.title: Four sheep slaughtered for two loaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא טירתא teaches a ברייתא: if four sheep were slaughtered with the two loaves of שבועות, two are sprinkled not for their own sake, so the other two are not lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא טירתא taught before רבי יוחנן: If someone slaughtered four sheep with the two loaves, he takes two of them aside and sprinkles their blood not for their own sake. Because if you don't say this, you have ruined the last two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about what to do if four sheep were slaughtered for שבועות when only two were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only two sheep go with the two loaves. The ברייתא says to sprinkle two of them first שלא לשמן, and then the other two can be sprinkled for their real purpose. If the first two were sprinkled for their real purpose, the last two would lose their chance and be ruined.

keyTerms.meaning: Sheep. Here, the two sheep brought together with the two loaves on שבועות.
The two loaves (שתי הלחם) brought on שבועות.
Not for their own sake, meaning not for the purpose they were set aside for.
You have caused a loss; you have ruined.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is NOT saying the first two sheep become invalid. It says to sprinkle them for a different purpose on purpose, so that the last two can still be used for שבועות.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טִירָתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina Tirata taught before Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט אַרְבָּעָה כְּבָשִׂים עַל שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת –
phrases.english: If one slaughtered four sheep along with two loaves,
phrases.notes: Only two sheep are supposed to come with the two loaves of שבועות, so two here are extra.

phrases.english: he draws two of them aside,
and sprinkles their blood not for their own sake.
For if you do not say this,
you have caused the loss of the last ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טִירָתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the sheep and loaves of שבועות, separate from the תודה loaves discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When four sheep were slaughtered for the two loaves, two are sprinkled not for their own sake first, so the remaining two can still be sprinkled for their real purpose and are not lost.

steps.title: Do we tell someone to sin so he can gain?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects: sprinkling blood not for its own sake on purpose is a sin, and we don't tell a person to sin so that he can gain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Do we really tell a person, 'Go and sin so that you will gain'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back on the ברייתא. He says the solution it gives is wrong because it asks the כהן to do something improper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling blood שלא לשמן on purpose is not allowed. The ברייתא suggests doing it anyway to save the other two sheep. רבי יוחנן says that saving something is not a good enough reason to tell someone to do a wrong act.

keyTerms.meaning: Go and sin so that you will gain. A principle that we don't ask someone to do wrong in order to benefit.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle: we don't permit a forbidden act just to avoid a loss. In the next steps רבי יוחנן backs it up with a משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
And do we say to a person,
"Get up and sin so that you will gain"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אוֹמֵר לוֹ לְאָדָם עֲמוֹד וַחֲטָא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּזְכֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's instruction to sprinkle two sheep שלא לשמן on purpose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doing the service שלא לשמן on purpose is wrong, and we don't tell a person to do wrong just to avoid losing the other animals.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה about mixed limbs to back his objection
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן supports his objection by quoting a משנה about limbs of a חטאת mixed with limbs of an עולה, where רבי אליעזר and חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: If limbs of a חטאת got mixed up with limbs of an עולה, רבי אליעזר says: put them all up on the מזבח, and I look at the meat of the חטאת on top as if it were wood. And חכמים say: let them sit until their form spoils, and then they go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן continues his objection by quoting a משנה. This sets up his point in the next step: the חכמים there do not allow sinning in order to gain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת's limbs may not be burned on the מזבח, but an עולה's limbs must be. רבי אליעזר lets the כהן put the mixed limbs on the מזבח, treating the חטאת meat like wood, so the עולה is not lost. The חכמים refuse and let everything spoil and be burned in the place of burning, even though the עולה is lost. רבי יוחנן will use their view as his proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The limbs of a חטאת (sin offering), which are eaten by כהנים and not burned on the מזבח.
A burnt offering, which is burned entirely on the מזבח.
That got mixed up together.
Let their form spoil, meaning wait until the meat goes bad overnight.
The place of burning, where invalid קדשים are burned.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר is not saying the חטאת meat really is wood. He is saying we can look at it as if it were wood, so putting it on the מזבח is allowed in order to save the עולה.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Limbs of a sin offering that got mixed with limbs of a burnt offering,
Rabbi Eliezer says: they should be placed up on the altar,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה to back up his objection in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא טירתא's ruling (step 10) that two sheep are sprinkled שלא לשמן to save the other two.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים in the משנה do not allow putting חטאת limbs on the מזבח, even though doing so would save the עולה. This supports רבי יוחנן's claim that we do not tell a person to sin so that he can gain.

steps.title: Why don't the חכמים let him sin in order to gain?
steps.stepSummary: Using the opinion of the חכמים in the משנה about mixed limbs, רבי יוחנן asks: if we really say 'sin so that you may gain,' why don't the חכמים allow burning everything on the מזבח?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do the חכמים say the mixture is burned? Let us tell the כהן: 'Arise and sin so that you may gain!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his proof from the משנה in step 12. The חכמים there clearly do not let a person sin in order to gain, so why should רבי חנינא טירתא allow it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mixed-limbs case, putting all the limbs on the מזבח would mean sinning with the חטאת limbs, but it would let the עולה limbs be offered. The חכמים still say the whole mixture goes to be burned, not offered. So it seems we never say 'sin so that you may gain,' which supports רבי יוחנן's objection in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Arise and sin so that you may gain: doing a small wrong in order to save a bigger מצוה
Why?
Let him say / we should say

phrases.english: Why? Let him say:
phrases.notes: He means: why do the חכמים in that משנה say the mixed limbs must be burned and not offered?

phrases.english: "Arise and sin so that you may gain"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? לֵימָא: עֲמוֹד וַחֲטָא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּזְכֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה in step 12, using the opinion of the חכמים against רבי חנינא טירתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא טירתא's ruling that two sheep are sprinkled שלא לשמן to save the other two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים refuse to let the limbs be offered even though sinning would gain the עולה. That shows we do not say 'sin so that you may gain.'

steps.title: Same offering yes, different offering no
steps.stepSummary: We say 'sin so that you may gain' when the sin and the gain are in the same kind of offering, but not when you sin with one offering to gain another.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Arise and sin with a חטאת so that you may gain with a חטאת,' we do say. 'Arise and sin with a חטאת so that you may gain with an עולה,' we do not say.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא טירתא answers by drawing a line. The mixed-limbs case is different from his case of the שבועות sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mixed-limbs case, the sin is with the חטאת but the gain is with the עולה, which is a different offering, so we do not allow it. In the case of the four sheep, the sin and the gain are both with the same offering, the sheep of שבועות. That is why sinning to gain is allowed there.

keyTerms.meaning: We say (we apply this rule)
Sin offering
Burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The key rule here: you may sin to gain within the same offering, but not across two different offerings.

phrases.english: Arise and sin with a sin offering
so that you may gain with a sin offering: we do say,
arise and sin with a sin offering
so that you may gain with a burnt offering: we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲמוֹד וַחֲטָא בְּחַטָּאת בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּזְכֶּה בְּחַטָּאת – אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (same offering vs. different offerings)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to reject 'sin so that you may gain' completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים only reject it when the sin and the gain are in different offerings. Within one offering, like the שבועות sheep, it is allowed.

steps.title: Do we say it even within one offering? The ברייתא of the שבועות sheep
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether we really say 'sin so that you may gain' even within one offering, and quotes a ברייתא about the כבשי עצרת slaughtered with the wrong intent or at the wrong time, and what happens when it is שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And within one matter, do we say it? But it was taught: the sheep of עצרת that were slaughtered not for their own sake, or slaughtered before or after their time, the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten. If it was שבת, he should not sprinkle. If he did sprinkle, it is accepted, so the אימורין may be burned in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the distinction from step 14 and starts quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא is the setup for his proof; the שבת part will be the key point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that when the day is שבת, we do not sprinkle the blood of these sheep, even though sprinkling would let the offering be eaten. It does not say 'sin with this offering so that you may gain with it.' So it seems we do not say it even within one offering, which goes against רבי חנינא טירתא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: One matter: the sin and the gain in the same offering
The two sheep brought on שבועות together with the two loaves
Not for their own sake: with the intent of a different offering
It is accepted (the offering works after the fact)
The fats and parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This step only quotes the ברייתא. The actual punch of the question (that we do not tell him to sprinkle on שבת so he can gain) comes right after.

phrases.english: And in one matter, do we say it?
phrases.notes: He means: do we really tell someone to sin so he can gain, even when it is all the same offering?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
the sheep of Shavuot that one slaughtered not for their own sake,
or that one slaughtered

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי זְמַנָּן בֵּין לְאַחַר זְמַנָּן –
phrases.english: either before their time or after their time:
phrases.notes: Their time is the day of שבועות itself.

phrases.english: the blood shall be sprinkled and the meat shall be eaten.
And if it was Shabbat, he should not sprinkle.
And if he did sprinkle, it is accepted
to burn the sacrificial portions in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַחֲדָא מִילְּתָא מִי אָמַר? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction just given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'sin so that you may gain' is said within the same offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On שבת the ברייתא says not to sprinkle, even though sprinkling would let the offering be completed. So we do not say 'sin so that you may gain' even within one offering.

steps.title: Why not sprinkle the blood of the כבשי עצרת on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes his question from the ברייתא. If we say 'sin so that you may gain,' the blood should be sprinkled on שבת so that the meat can later be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why not? Let us say: 'Get up and sin so that you can gain!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes the challenge he started in step 15. The ברייתא says that on שבת we do not sprinkle the blood of a כבשי עצרת that was slaughtered with the wrong intent. He asks why we don't just tell the כהן to sin so that he can gain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the sin and the gain are in the same offering. That is exactly the case where step 14 said we do say 'sin so that you may gain.' Sprinkling the blood on שבת would be a sin, but it would let the parts be burned and the meat be eaten. Yet the ברייתא does not allow it, so the rule from step 14 seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Get up and sin so that you may gain.' Telling someone to do a small wrong so that something good comes out of it.
'Let us say.' It suggests what should have been said.
Why?

phrases.english: But why?
phrases.notes: He means: why does the ברייתא say not to sprinkle the blood on שבת?

phrases.english: Let us say: 'Get up and sin'
'so that you may gain!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא: עֲמוֹד חֲטָא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתִּזְכֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 15 began by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 14, that we do say 'sin so that you may gain' within one offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא the sin and the gain are in one offering, yet the blood is not sprinkled on שבת. That goes against step 14's rule.

steps.title: The sin and the gain must both be on שבת
steps.stepSummary: We say 'sin so that you may gain' only when both the sin and the gain happen on שבת. We do not say it when you sin on שבת and gain only on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sin on שבת so that you gain on שבת': we say that. 'Sin on שבת so that you gain on a weekday': we don't say that.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to רבי יוחנן's question. The rule only works when the sin and the gain happen on the same kind of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the כבשי עצרת, sprinkling the blood would be a sin on שבת. The gain, burning the parts and eating the meat, would only come later on a weekday. Since the sin and the gain are on different days, we do not tell him to sin, so the ברייתא fits.

keyTerms.meaning: A weekday, a regular day that is not שבת.
'We say' / 'we don't say.' Whether a rule is applied or not.

steps.whatToRemember: 'Sin so that you may gain' needs the sin and the gain to match: the same offering (step 14) and the same day (here).

phrases.english: 'Get up and sin on שבת'
'so that you gain on שבת': we say that.
'Get up and sin on שבת'
'so that you gain on a weekday': we don't say that.
phrases.notes: Here the gain is burning the parts and eating the meat, which would only happen after שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲמוֹד חֲטָא בְּשַׁבָּת כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּזְכֶּה בְּשַׁבָּת אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16's challenge by adding a new limit to the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a condition: the sin and the gain must happen at the same time (both on שבת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the sin and the gain are in one offering, we should say 'sin so that you may gain' even on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gain only comes on a weekday, so the rule does not apply, and the blood is not sprinkled on שבת.

steps.title: A challenge from the broken barrel of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we really never say 'sin so that you may gain' for two separate matters. It quotes a משנה: if a barrel of תרומה breaks in the upper winepress and there is impure חולין below, everyone agrees that one should save a רביעית of the תרומה in purity. The quote then begins רבי אליעזר's view for the case where that is not possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for two separate things, don't we say it? But we learned in a משנה: a barrel of תרומה broke in the upper winepress, and in the lower one there is impure חולין. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that if he can save a רביעית of it in purity, he should save it. And if not, רבי אליעזר says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 14 that we don't say 'sin so that you may gain' across two separate matters. It quotes a משנה about spilled תרומה wine, and the quote keeps going into the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he saves the רביעית, the rest of the תרומה flows down into the impure חולין and becomes impure, which is a kind of sin. The gain is the small amount he saves. The loss and the gain involve two different portions of wine, yet the משנה says to save it, which suggests we do say 'sin so that you may gain' even for two matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Two separate matters or things.
The portion of produce given to a כהן. It is holy and must be kept pure.
Regular, non-holy produce that is impure.
A winepress. This one has an upper section and a lower section.
A quarter of a לוג, a small liquid measure.
In purity, kept ritually pure (in a pure vessel).

steps.confusionAlert: The 'gain' here is not money. Meanwhile, the rest of the תרומה flows down and becomes impure. The gain is saving even a small amount of תרומה while it is still pure.

phrases.english: And for two separate matters, doesn't one say it?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about step 14's idea: sinning with one thing to gain with another.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
A barrel of תרומה wine that broke
in the upper winepress,
and in the lower one there is impure חולין wine:
phrases.notes: The spilled תרומה will run down into the lower press and become impure.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree
that if he is able to save from it
a רביעית in purity, he should save it.
And if not,
phrases.notes: He means: if he cannot save any of it in purity.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
phrases.notes: His view continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 14's idea, that we don't say the rule across two matters, and challenges it with a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 14's claim that 'sin so that you may gain' is not said when the sin and the gain involve two separate things.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, letting the rest of the תרומה become impure (the sin) is allowed so that a separate רביעית can be saved (the gain). That shows we do say the rule across two matters.
